hook.line: The partnership is signed, and Vale deserves more than a nod. In English you congratulate someone on something. Spanish uses a different little word.

examples.en: Congratulations on your graduation! (to a friend)
Congratulations to the bride and groom!

rule:
*¡Felicitaciones!* or *¡Felicidades!* works for anything: a birthday, a wedding, a new job. Both are always plural.

To say what for, English uses on. Spanish uses *por*: *por el bebé*, *por tu graduación*. With an action, *por* + the plain verb: *por graduarte*, *por abrir el café*.

To say who, use *a*: *¡Felicitaciones a los novios!*

To a person directly, you can also say *Te felicito* (to a friend) or *Lo felicito*, *La felicito* (formal).
smallPrint: In Spain you'll hear *¡Enhorabuena!* for an achievement. In Colombia and most of Latin America, *felicitaciones* covers it.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *en* or *por* and type the whole line: *¡Felicitaciones ___ el trabajo nuevo!*
Pick *por* or *a* and type the whole line: *¡Felicitaciones ___ los novios!* (to the bride and groom)
Type in Spanish: Congratulations on the baby!
Type in Spanish, to a friend: Congratulations on graduating!
yourTurn.why: After *por*, an action stays in its plain form, with *te* on the end.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Congratulations on the new apartment!
yourTurn.why: Same frame, new thing: *por el apartamento nuevo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it straight to a friend instead: *¡Felicitaciones por el trabajo nuevo!* (use *felicito*)
yourTurn.answer: Te felicito por el trabajo nuevo.
yourTurn.why: *Te felicito* is I congratulate you; the *por* stays.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish congratulates you *por* something, not *en* it.
As a greeting it's always plural.
After *por*, use the plain verb, not a past form.

personal: Think of someone who had good news lately and congratulate them in Spanish with *por*.
